title: Affine function-field presentation of the Bertini incidence scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a scheme of finite type over $k$ which is geometrically irreducible over $k$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $V$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ a $k$-linear map. Assume (i) there are $v_1,v_2,v_3\in V$ and an irreducible component $W$ of $H_{v_2}\cap H_{v_3}$ with $W\not\subseteq H_{v_1}$ and $\operatorname{codim}(W,Y)=2$; (ii) every irreducible component $B$ of $\bigcap_{v\in V}H_v$ has $\operatorname{codim}(B,Y)\ge2$. Fix any basis b of V and let q be its universal incidence projection of [def-zl-bertini-universal-family]. There exist a finite type k-domain A, n>=2 and g_1,...,g_n in A such that V(g_1,g_2) has a component W with dim W+2=dim A, Spec Frac A is geometrically irreducible over k, the universal incidence scheme H is irreducible, q is dominant, and the spectrum of its generic residue-field map Spec kappa(genericPoint H) -> Spec kappa(q(genericPoint H)) is isomorphic, as an arrow of schemes, to Spec Omega -> Spec F, where Omega=Frac(Frac(A)[x_1,...,x_n]) and F=k(x_1,...,x_n,sum_i g_i x_i), as in [lem-zl-bertini-field-extension]. The statement asserts an actual arrow isomorphism, not geometric irreducibility of Omega/F. Dimensions, fields and fibres are as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Conventions: schemes and their residue fields [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], finite type and quasi-compact morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], section zero schemes [def-pc-zero-scheme], geometric irreducibility [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: First replace $Y$ by $Y_{\mathrm{red}}$ and restrict $\mathcal L$ and its sections. Indeed $Y$ is quasi-compact (finite type over a field), and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes it locally Noetherian, since a field has only two ideals. By [lem-sc-reduction-nilradical-nilpotent], its nilradical ideal sheaf $N$ has a positive power zero. After any field extension, the image of $N$ still has that power zero; quotienting further by any section equation preserves this. Prime ideals all contain a nilpotent ideal, so the thickenings $Y_{\mathrm{red},k'}\to Y_{k'}$ and their section zero schemes have identical underlying spaces. The same holds for the intersections in (i) and (ii); their components and codimensions agree. Thus all hypotheses and the desired geometric irreducibility are unchanged. The reduced, irreducible scheme is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. On every affine open its ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. The corresponding nilpotent closed immersion on universal incidence schemes also identifies their underlying spaces and all residue fields, compatibly with the projection maps. Thus irreducibility, dominance and the generic residue-field arrow transfer back to the original possibly nonreduced Y.

proof.text: The vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3$ in (i) are linearly independent. A relation $a_1v_1+a_2v_2+a_3v_3=0$, evaluated in the fibre of $\mathcal L$ at the generic point of $W$, forces $a_1=0$: the first section is nonzero there, while the other two vanish there. If $v_2,v_3$ were dependent, their zero-scheme intersection would be either all of $Y$ or the zero scheme of one section. The first case has no component of codimension two. In the second, on an affine trivializing neighbourhood of the generic point of $W$, its prime is minimal over one local equation. The image prime in the quotient is minimal, hence height zero; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $t=1$ gives height at most one. Heights compute the codimensions here by the prime/irreducible-closed-subset correspondence, contradicting (i). Extend these vectors to a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ of $V$, with $r\geq3$.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, first proof paragraph: the omitted linear-independence detail

proof.text: On an affine chart with a free line-bundle generator, apply lem-zl-bertini-affine-incidence-chart. It gives the actual polynomial quotient presentation of the universal incidence scheme, together with its map to coefficient affine space. Restriction to a trivializing affine open is the base change of the universal family. The coefficient formula and the canonical affine ambient pullback are proved in that chart theorem. Finiteness of a trivializing affine cover follows from quasi-compactness; its quotient charts are finite type over coefficient affine space.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, first two proof paragraphs; Varieties Situation 0G47

proof.text: On each such nonempty chart $U$, $f_1\ne0$. To see this, $\psi(v_1)$ is nonzero at the generic point of $W$ by (i), so it is not the zero section. On an integral scheme a section of a line bundle which vanishes on a nonempty open vanishes everywhere: in intersecting trivializing charts this is the injectivity of a domain into its fraction field, and multiplying by invertible transition functions preserves zero. Hypothesis (ii) says that each minimal prime of $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ has height at least two; components of the base locus meeting $U$ are precisely these primes, and their local rings and chains of generalizations are unchanged on restriction to $U$. Apply [lem-zl-bertini-affine-incidence-irreducible] to obtain irreducibility of each $H_U$. For two nonempty base charts, their intersection is nonempty because the base is irreducible. The proved zero-coefficient section Y -> H supplies a point of the intersection of the incidence charts over any point of this base intersection. Thus the irreducible open incidence charts pairwise intersect and cover H, proving H irreducible. No localization at a unit coefficient is needed for this gluing argument.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, middle proof paragraph: irreducibility of the universal incidence scheme

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y\setminus H_{v_1}$ meeting $W$. Use $\psi(v_1)$ itself to trivialize $\mathcal L$ there; write the other sections as $g_2,\ldots,g_r$, so the universal equation is $x_1+\sum_{i=2}^r g_ix_i=0$. The component $W\cap U$ of $V(g_2,g_3)$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak p$ of height two. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring], every maximal prime chain in $A$ has the same finite length $d=\dim A$. Extend a saturated length-two chain from $(0)$ to $\mathfrak p$ by any maximal chain above it; the concatenation is maximal in $A$, so every such upper chain has length $d-2$. Prime correspondence for $A/\mathfrak p$ gives $\dim(W\cap U)=d-2$. Hence [lem-zl-bertini-independent-functions] applies to $g_2,\ldots,g_r$ and supplies $c_2,\ldots,c_r$ for which $x_2,\ldots,x_r,\xi=\sum_{i=2}^r g_ix_i,\delta=\sum_{i=2}^r c_ig_i$ are algebraically independent over $k$ in $\Omega=K(x_2,\ldots,x_r)$, where $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, last proof paragraph; Tag 0G4E; Tag 00OS chain-length formula

proof.text: Apply the generic-residue-field criterion to the geometrically irreducible Y and identify its generic residue field with Frac A on the chosen integral affine chart. This proves the asserted geometric irreducibility of Frac A over k.

Use the independent-functions theorem to obtain independence of the variables and the universal linear combination. Thus the parameter map into A[x_2,...,x_r] is injective and q is dominant. Apply lem-zl-bertini-incidence-elimination with its substitution formula to eliminate the first variable. The incidence generic residue field is Frac(Frac(A)[x_2,...,x_r]); the parameter residue field maps isomorphically onto k(x_2,...,x_r,sum g_i x_i), with the sign absorbed by a variable automorphism. These identify the required residue-field arrow. Transport across the invertible linear coordinate change from the adapted basis to b and across the ULift renaming. No geometric irreducibility of the incidence field or generic-fibre assertion is used.

theorem exists_bertiniIncidenceChart
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (L : Y.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] :
    letI : Module k Γ(L, ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom Γ(L, ⊤) (Scheme.globalSectionsRingHom k (X := Y))
    ∀ ψ : V →ₗ[k] Γ(L, ⊤),
      (∃ (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (W : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y),
        Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y ↦
          (Z : Set Y) ⊆ (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₂)).zeroLocus.support ∩
            (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₃)).zeroLocus.support) W ∧
        ¬ (W : Set Y) ⊆ (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₁)).zeroLocus.support ∧
        Order.coheight W = 2) →
      (∀ B : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y,
        Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y ↦
          (Z : Set Y) ⊆ ⋂ w : V,
            ((Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ w)).zeroLocus.support : Set Y)) B →
        2 ≤ Order.coheight B) →
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) k V),
        let H := (bertiniUniversalIdeal (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) L
          (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ ψ (b i.down))).subscheme
        let q := bertiniUniversalProjection (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) L
          (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ ψ (b i.down))
        ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (a : Algebra k A),
          letI := a
          ∃ (hft : Algebra.FiniteType k A) (hdom : IsDomain A),
            letI := hft
            letI := hdom
            ∃ (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (g : Fin n → A),
              (∃ W : Set (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
                  ({g ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hn⟩, g ⟨1, hn⟩} : Set A)),
                W ∈ irreducibleComponents (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
                  ({g ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hn⟩, g ⟨1, hn⟩} : Set A)) ∧
                topologicalKrullDim W + 2 = ringKrullDim A) ∧
              GeometricallyIrreducible
                (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (FractionRing A)))) ∧
              ∃ hI : IrreducibleSpace H,
                letI := hI
                IsDominant q ∧ Nonempty (Arrow.mk
                  (Spec.map (q.residueFieldMap (genericPoint H))) ≅
                  Arrow.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
                    (algebraMap
                      (FieldTheory.bertiniBaseField k (FractionRing A) n
                        (fun i ↦ algebraMap A (FractionRing A) (g i)))
                      (FieldTheory.bertiniOmega (FractionRing A) n)))))
